`createPiDurableExtension` receives `{ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log, images }`:

| Option | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `cwd` | The workspace |
| `agentDir` | `agent_dir`, resolved against the workspace. If `agent_dir` is empty: a new temporary directory in `RUNNER_TEMP` |
| `trustProject` | The `trust_project` input |
| `ui` | `{ ask, notify }`, the GitHub UI (see [Questions on GitHub](#questions-on-github)). Only in `comment` mode on an issue or pull request. Not set in `output` mode or for direct prompts |
| `log` | The log of the action (`info`, `warning`) |
| `images` | An image processor, `createNodePhotonImages()` of pi-durable. It resizes and converts images to the limits of the model, for example for pit's `workspace.viewImage` (pit 0.36.2 and later) |

pi-durable extensions run in the process of pi-action. Thus, pi-action also sets `GH_TOKEN` and the git identity in its own environment when it loads such an extension. See [Security](security.md#the-agents-github-token-and-git-identity).

### Show tool calls in the workflow log

A tool can say how the [workflow log](how-it-works.md#the-workflow-log) shows its calls. Give the tool an optional `present` field. pi-durable does not use it, so other hosts ignore it. pit's `typescript` tool has one (pit 0.36.5 and later): the log shows the label of each program, its code, the functions it uses, and its result as text:

```ts
// pi-durable's types do not declare `present`: add it to the tool that defineTool() returns.
const tool = {
	...defineTool({ name: "typescript" /* ... */ }),
	present: {
		// When the call starts: the 🔧 line, and the details in place of the arguments.
		call: (args) => ({ title: args.label, body: args.code }),
		// When it ends: the ↳ line in place of "N lines", and the details in place of the output.
		result: (args, result) => ({ summary: "workspace.read", body: "..." }),
	},
};
```

- `call(args)` gets the arguments of the call. It returns `{ title, body? }`. `title` must not be empty.
- `result(args, result)` gets the arguments and the stored tool result (pi-ai's `ToolResultMessage`, with its `details`). It returns `{ summary?, body? }`.
- Both functions are optional. Each field that a function leaves out gets the usual form.
- Return plain text, synchronously. Use only the inputs: pi-action calls the functions for the stored entries of the conversation, not while the tool runs.
- pi-action keeps its limits: one line of at most 120 characters for `title` and `summary`, 4000 characters of `body` for a call, and the last 30 lines of `body` for a result. It also stops the runner from running workflow commands in the text.
- If a function throws or returns another type, pi-action shows the usual form, and writes `⚠️ Tool <name>: present.call() failed ...` to the log one time.
- A tool that replaces an earlier one with the same name also replaces its `present`.

8. **Report.** For each request, pi-action posts a `🤖 pi Response` comment (or `❌ pi Error`), and adds 🚀 (or 😕) to the request. If pi gives an empty answer, pi-action asks one time for a summary. If a response hits the output token limit (`max_tokens`) without a tool call, pi-action asks pi to continue, up to 3 times in a row and within `timeout`, and then posts an error. In `output` mode, pi-action sets the `response` and `success` outputs and posts nothing.
9. **Save.** pi-action pushes the thread. Each comment of pi-action ends with a collapsed `🧵 This conversation is stored in git on ...` section with the git commands that read the thread. The workflow log shows them too. See [Read a thread](threads.md#read-a-thread).

When a tool from a pi-durable extension asks a question, the run ends after step 7 without a `pi Response` comment. See [Questions on GitHub](extensions.md#questions-on-github).

## The workflow log

The log of the `Run pi-action` step shows what pi does while it works, one line for each step. Click a line with a `▸` to see its details. A run that answers one comment looks like this:

```text
▸ Setup
🤖 nvidia/aws/anthropic/bedrock-claude-opus-5-5 · thinking medium · tools: read, write, edit, bash, typescript · extensions: pit (typescript)
▸ 🧵 Thread refs/pi/threads/46: continuing, started 2026-11-12 07:11 UTC
▶ Request from @cv (https://github.com/o/r/issues/46#issuecomment-1): Ready to write a PR?
💬 I'll look at the existing sessions first.
🔧 bash: git log --oneline -5
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.1s · 5 lines
🔧 edit: src/run.ts (2 edits)
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.0s · 1 line
🔧 Read the run tests
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.1s · 412 lines
▸ 💬 I opened PR #48, which ...
✅ Replied: https://github.com/o/r/issues/46#issuecomment-2 (24 model responses · 23 tool calls · 6m40s · 2.1M tokens in, 31k out)
🧵 refs/pi/threads/46 is at 4325d9a
```

| Line | What it shows | Details (`▸`) |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| `Setup` | | The extensions, prompt templates, and [skills](skills.md) that pi-action loaded, and the variables that the tools of pi get |
| `🤖` | The model, its thinking level (see [Thinking](models.md#thinking)), the tools that it gets (see [Tools the model sees](extensions.md#tools-the-model-sees)), and the pi-durable extensions with their tools | |
| `🧵 Thread` | The thread ref, and if the thread is new or continues | The git commands that read the thread ([Read a thread](threads.md#read-a-thread)) |
| `▶` | A request that pi gets: who asked, where, and its first line. For a [prompt template](prompts.md#prompt-templates) or a [skill](skills.md#use-a-skill-explicitly), the line as typed and where it comes from | |
| `💬` | The text of a model response (its first line, if it is longer) | The full text |
| `🔧` | A tool call, when it starts. For a call with a `label` argument, only the label. For other calls, the tool and its main argument (the command or the path). For a script of more than one line, the first line and the number of other lines. A tool can show its own text instead (see [Show tool calls in the workflow log](extensions.md#show-tool-calls-in-the-workflow-log)) | |
| `↳ ✓` or `↳ ✗ failed` | The end of a tool call: how long it took, and how many lines of output it gave. A tool can show its own text instead (see [Show tool calls in the workflow log](extensions.md#show-tool-calls-in-the-workflow-log)) | The arguments (long JSON values indented), and the last 30 lines of output |
| `✅ Replied` or `❌ Reported the error` | The comment, and totals for the reply: model responses, tool calls, time, tokens, and cost if the provider reports it | |
| `🧵 … is at` | The commit of the thread ref after the last push | |

pi-action writes each push of the thread and each snapshot of the working tree as debug messages. To see them, [enable step debug logging](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/enable-debug-logging) and run the job again. Warnings and errors always show.

## Commit conventions

pi-action installs no git hooks and does not check commit messages. pi follows the conventions of your repository:

- Your own git hooks (for example from husky, lefthook, or prek) run when pi commits, if your workflow installs them before pi-action.
- Write your commit format in `AGENTS.md`. pi-action puts it into the system prompt (see [The system prompt](prompts.md#the-system-prompt)). pi reads other files, such as `CONTRIBUTING.md`, with its tools; link to them from `AGENTS.md`.
- To enforce a commit format, check it in your repository, for example with a CI job. pi can skip hooks with `git commit --no-verify`, so only a check outside the checkout enforces a format.
--- PR 397
feat(durable): collapse finished runs' tool calls to their labels after each run
Refs #396. Acceptance needs a release and a live pi-action thread, so this PR doesn't close the issue.

## What it does

After every run that answers, pi-durable hosts collapse the tool calls of older finished runs into one deterministic line each. No model call is involved. The line is written in the same `afterRun` write that applies the edits the model staged during the run, so there's still a single `pit.context-edit` entry per run:

```
[Pit: collapsed typescript call · "Read npm and git global and command sources" · workspace.read, workspace.search · ok · ~18.2K tokens · originals: session.inspectEntry("212"), session.inspectEntry("213")]
```

- **Label:** the `// @pit:` header or the `label` argument, else the program's first line, resolved the same way as `present.call`. The functions come from the same parsing `present.result` uses. The outcome is `ok`, `failed: <error's first line>`, `asked: <title>`, `saved <name>`, or `no result`. For other tools the line gives the tool name and the outcome. An entry with several calls lists each one, separated by `;`.
- **Shape:** the assistant entry keeps its text and thinking, signatures included. Its tool calls become the line and its results are omitted, so no call is left unanswered and no result is orphaned. The pairing is the same as `elide`.
- **Never touched:** user and host messages, answers, compaction summaries, notes, entries already rewritten or with a staged edit, entries no larger than their line, and the current run. A model `elide` or `summarize` staged in the same run wins, and the collapse skips its targets.
- **Provenance:** `operation: "collapse"` sits next to the model's `elide`/`summarize` operations. `session.outline()` shows collapsed entries as `elided`, with the line as the preview. I didn't add a new outline state, because `PitContextState` is shared with Pi's global contract. `inspectEntry` still returns every original.
- **Runs:** a run starts at the user or host messages that follow the previous run's entries. Everything from `run.first` onward is the current run. The view is read from the active range in the same commit, so the collapse never crosses the newest compaction head, and a fork keeps the view it had at its fork point.
- **Guideline:** when collapse is on, `pit_guidelines` gains this line: "Calls from finished runs collapse to their labels: give each call a specific label, and say in your answer what a later run will need."

## Defaults (a behaviour change, listed in CHANGELOG)

- **On by default:** `collapse: { keepRuns: 1, minTokens: 32_000 }`. pi-action is the main durable host and runs headless, so nobody follows Pit's context-pressure notices there. `collapse: false` turns it off.
- **`keepRuns: 1`** counts the run that just answered. The follow-up usually refers to that run, so it stays whole and older runs collapse.
- **`minTokens: 32_000`** counts the conversation's messages only, not the system prompt, tools, and sections. On pi-action those fixed parts are about 41K tokens, so a floor on the whole context would always be exceeded. Below about 32K the transcript is smaller than the fixed prompt, so collapsing would cut a cold follow-up by less than half while losing verbatim history. Above it the transcript dominates. Thread #383's 170K prompt was far past it.

## Line bound

Each line is at most 512 bytes. Labels and outcomes are first cut to 160 characters each. If the line is still too long, the injected function list goes first, then the description is cut at its end with `…`. The token size and the `inspectEntry` IDs are never cut. When the usual form doesn't fit, the IDs switch to `session.inspectEntry(id) for "212", "213"`. An entry with so many parallel calls that its IDs alone pass 512 bytes keeps all its IDs and names no calls.

## Strict-provider check

I ran this with pi-ai's `anthropic-messages` API against `aws/anthropic/bedrock-claude-opus-5-5` on `https://inference-api.nvidia.com`, the route pi-action uses, with adaptive thinking:

- **Accepted:** user, then two collapsed tool-calling turns in a row (each `thinking` with its real signature + `text` + collapsed line, `stopReason: stop`), then the answer, then a follow-up. That's three assistant messages in a row. Also accepted: the same without thinking, and a later run's live tool call and result after a collapsed run. So I kept the issue's shape and did not merge adjacent assistant messages.
- **With the guideline** in the system prompt, the model read the lines as its earlier calls: "it called echo twice: the transcript shows two collapsed echo-call markers, both marked ok…".
- **Without the guideline**, the model once said a collapsed line was "text I wrote myself". That's the reason the guideline ships with the feature.
- **Rejected:** sending the *same* signed thinking block twice, which I did only as an artificial copy. The request was blocked as "duplicating model outputs". The collapse never copies a block, because each entry keeps its own thinking.

`docs/durable.md` records this.

--- PR 401
fix(renderers): display labels and inputs from source headers
## Summary

TypeScript calls can supply labels and other options in a leading `// @pit: {...}` source header. Execution prepares these options, but terminal rendering receives the original arguments (including on replay) and previously looked only for a top-level label. This caused valid header labels to disappear in favor of inferred titles.

- Normalize terminal display arguments through the existing `applySourceOptions` parser, then omit null options, matching execution.
- Use the normalized arguments for call titles and expanded inputs, including params, function identity, save-only state, and timeout.
- Preserve raw arguments for inspection when a header is incomplete, malformed, unknown, or conflicting; do not mutate execution or stored data.
- Add renderer regressions and three offline Pi acceptance fixtures.

## Verification

- [x] Reproduced the missing-label bug: three regression cases failed with “Run workspace task” before the fix.
- [x] Reproduced missing structured header options in successful and failed expanded results before fixing input rendering.
- [x] 79 targeted renderer, extension, and durable presentation tests passed.
- [x] `delivery.validate({ coverage: true, packageCheck: true })`: check, tests, coverage, and package verification passed.
- [x] Real isolated Pi acceptance: dark/light themes, 60/80/120 columns, collapsed/expanded views, actual running-to-settled progress, rejected-header diagnostics, and reload.
- [x] Independent read-only Claude Opus 5.5 review: no blocking findings. This review was static and did not independently rerun validation or live acceptance.

### Non-blocking review notes

Applying a source header retains a leading blank line until display formatting completes. The reviewer also suggested optional coverage for null top-level options alongside a header and header-first streaming transitions. These are not required for the reported missing-label fix. Rejected headers intentionally remain visible in the terminal for inspection.

## Remote checks

- CI passed on Node 22, 24, and 26 for commit `67c680869fa84663e48e63fa9e80a0c1c70a5bde`: https://github.com/cv/pit/actions/runs/44098980808
- Dependency review passed.
- The separate `pi Assistant` workflow failed before running its review: GitHub App token creation received an empty `client-id`/`app-id` with `Secret source: None`. This is a workflow credential/context failure, not a renderer or test failure: https://github.com/cv/pit/actions/runs/44098980800
